meta.title: Library Book Holds
meta.headline: From a search to a book on the shelf at home
meta.source: Source: a made-up library, written to show every part of the format.

tabs.label: What a reader goes through
tabs.hint: Across: what happens to a hold. Down: who does each part.

labels.none: The source names nothing to build for this.

panel.title: What a reader goes through
text: A reader asks for a book, the library holds a copy, tells them it is ready, and they pick it up.
Click a box to read what it is. The boxes it connects to light up.

tagLegend.meaning: is needed and nothing does it yet.

lanes.name: The reader
lanes.none: Nothing to build. The reader does this.

panel.title: What the reader is sent
panel.text: Each message goes to the email and phone on the library card.

items.text: Finds the book and presses Hold
items.plain: The reader searches the catalogue and presses Hold on a title.

items.text: Puts them in the queue for that title
items.plain: The catalogue adds the reader to the end of the title's queue.
where: holds table, one row per request
notes: A reader can hold 10 titles at once.

items.text: Picks a copy and sets it aside
items.plain: When a copy is returned, the catalogue gives it to the first reader in the queue.

callouts.label: Built so far
callouts.text: Nearest-copy picking runs at two branches; the rest still pick by date.

parts.title: Chooses the copy
parts.text: The nearest branch with a copy on the shelf comes first.

parts.title: Moves it between branches
parts.label: Waits on
parts.text: The van schedule, which is being changed.

items.text: Puts it on the holds shelf
items.plain: Staff scan the copy and put it on the holds shelf under the reader's name.

items.text: Tells the reader it is ready
items.plain: An email and a text go out as soon as the copy is scanned onto the shelf.
Readers with the app also see the hold marked Ready.
The reader shows their card at the desk and takes the book.
If nobody collects it in 7 days, the copy goes to the next reader in the queue.

callouts.label: Not built yet
callouts.text: Today staff do this by hand each Monday.

items.text: Reminds them 2 days before it is due
items.plain: A due-soon email goes out 2 days before the return date.
Any branch takes it back; the catalogue then serves the next hold.

items.outcome: the Hold button explains the limit

items.detail: Staff mark it lost, and the catalogue picks another copy.

flags.p: The help page says holds are kept 7 days; the email says 5. One of them is out of date.
